Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i'm maya patel from redwood, i`ll run point on onboarding and sprints. um quick roll call?
[00:12] Derek: hey sorry, derek here — head of ml ops at abbeyworks.
[00:18] Sofia: sofia, vp product.
[00:22] Ibrahim: ibrahim, platform engineer. good to meet you all.
[00:26] Jon: jon reyes from implementation — i'll own the staging and infra bits.
[00:30] Priya: priya shah, solutions eng, i'll cover security and integration flows.
[00:35] Maya: awesome. quick agenda — two main goals: align on go-live date and success criteria, and map infra/security steps for private deployment. any additions?
[00:46] Derek: sounds good. we also want to validate latency for our customer-facing agent (peak qps ~200) and confirm data residency controls.
[00:55] Maya: perfect. so first — timeline. where are you all thinking? i remember you said q4 pilot?
[01:04] Sofia: yes, target pilot late september, but we'd like a closed beta in august if we can get a staging environment.
[01:12] Jon: ok that gives ~10 weeks. we usually run a 4-week staging + 4-week pilot cadence, leaves buffer for issues.
[01:20] Ibrahim: staging cluster must be private in our VPC; we can't send PII out of our region.
[01:26] Priya: we can do redwood private deployment into your VPC — it's our usual private control plane. we'll need a network diagram and allowed IP ranges, and we support KMS/HSM via customer key usage.
[01:38] Derek: great. what about audit logs — retention and export? we need six months of audit logs for compliance.
[01:45] Priya: audit logs are exportable to your S3; retention is configurable. we'll send the doc with fields and retention options. note: the cloud console shows token-level usage per request too.
[01:55] Sofia: curious on SSO — we use Okta. can we map RBAC roles from our groups?
[02:03] Maya: yes, we support SAML with group mapping — we'll include the SSO checklist.
[02:08] Ibrahim: network-wise, are we doing VPC peering or a VPN? some security folks insist on private interconnect.
[02:15] Jon: we can support VPC peering for lower latency; VPN is fallback. peering requires route tables and prefix lists, which we'll document.
[02:23] Derek: latency — earlier you shared benchmarks for 8k context models, but our agent uses 2k average and spikes to 5k. what's the expected p95?
[02:33] Priya: on our dedicated pools p95 for that profile is ~180-220ms for generation tokens assuming batching optimized; in private deployment we can tune autoscaling and kernel selection. note though, if you push batching for cost, tail latency can rise.
[02:48] Sofia: tradeoff we expected. our success criteria: for pilot we need p95 < 300ms for single-turn prompts and cost per 1k tokens under our budget.
[02:58] Maya: i'll capture that as a P0.
[03:02] Ibrahim: what about caching? can we do prefix caching? our product repeats a lot of prompts.
[03:08] Jon: yes, we can enable KV cache or prefix cache depending on model. we call it KV cache in docs but sometimes the transcription says KV cash.
[03:16] (laughter)
[03:18] Derek: hah, perfect. good note.
[03:21] Maya: operational play — we'll propose a sprint plan. week 1: infra and network, week 2: SSO & KMS, week 3: routing and scale tests, week 4: beta handoff, then pilot. does that align?
[03:34] Sofia: yes that maps. do you have a template for the runbook?
[03:38] Maya: yep will share. it has checklists for allowlists, certs, KMS key creation, and smoke tests.
[03:45] Ibrahim: for tests, can we run a short baseline latency test in staging before we onboard real prompts? we want the raw numbers to compare to your published profile.
[03:53] Jon: i'll run a p50/p95/p99 sweep and share results in a spreadsheet. expecting to run 10k calls across different sequence lengths.
[04:02] Derek: ok. question on backups — do you keep any customer text logs by default? we need zero retention in staging.
[04:10] Priya: default is configurable — you can opt-out of request logging, or set a null sink. we'll document the exact env variables.
[04:17] Sofia: regarding costs, if we need a dedicated pool for the pilot, what's the pricing model? reserved vs burst?
[04:25] Maya: for pilot we recommend borrowed dedicated capacity with a short commitment — we can offer ramped pricing. i'll follow up with numbers, but we can also start hosted and move to private when ready.
[04:37] Derek: due to compliance we prefer private, but cost will be a factor. comparing to Anthropic offerings was brought up by procurement, any remarks?
[04:46] Priya: we see Anthropic strong on safety models but our differentiation is production tooling — transparent token-level cost, smart routing, and observability per-route. plus easy private plane integration for regulated customers.
[04:57] Sofia: great. small ask — can you show a short demo of the control plane and how the model pinning looks?
[05:03] Priya: yeah, i'll schedule a 20-minute demo next week to walk the VPC console, model catalog, and rollout policies.
[05:10] Maya: next week works — priya, jon, can you both do that?
[05:14] Jon: yes.
[05:15] Priya: yes.
[05:17] Maya: ok moving on — dependencies: abbeyworks needs to share network diagram, allowlists, Okta admin contact, and sample prompt set. we'll need that to start.
[05:28] Derek: i'll share the network diagram and security contact after this call.
[05:31] Sofia: i'll coordinate product's prompt set.
[05:33] Ibrahim: i'll provide allowed IP ranges and infra owner details.
[05:36] Maya: perfect. i'll also attach a security pack: SOC2 summary, ISO status, and our KMS/HSM integration notes.
[05:45] (short pause)
[06:00] Priya: a couple of gotchas from previous customers — if you plan on long contexts we need to pick the right kernel and quantization strategy; sometimes quantization saves cost but increases sampling variability.
[06:13] Derek: noted. we can experiment in staging. what about model versioning and rollbacks? if we do a canary and rollout and see regressions, how fast is rollback?
[06:23] Jon: rollbacks are fast — model pinning and instant route switch to previous variant; we've got safe fallbacks configured. we also keep canary traffic small for the first 24 hours.
[06:33] Sofia: do you support function/tool calling in the runtime? we have a structured output pipeline.
[06:40] Priya: yes, function calling is supported; we also have structured output validation hooks you can run in the pipeline.
[06:46] Derek: ok good. any preliminary docs we should read?
[06:50] Maya: i'll drop links in the follow-up — onboarding runbook, private deployment checklist, and a short benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:57] Ibrahim: will the staging cluster be accessible via our jumpbox or do we need VPN?
[07:02] Jon: we'll set up access via your jumpbox, or if you prefer, direct peering. we'll include both options in the network playbook.
[07:10] Sofia: offline question on billing — can we split billing to a separate cost center? our finance wants separate invoicing for pilots.
[07:17] Maya: yes, we can set billing contact and invoice codes; i'll include the billing form.
[07:22] Derek: Anything else?
[07:24] Maya: i think that's the major items. to summarize: deliverables from redwood: runbook + security pack (maya), staging pool + baseline tests (jon), control plane demo (priya). deliverables from abbeyworks: network diagram, allowlist, okta admin, prompt set. pilot runway is september with closed beta earlier.
[07:46] Sofia: sounds good.
[07:48] Derek: yes.
[07:50] Maya: i'll record action items in crm and ping everyone. final check — any blockers?
[07:58] Ibrahim: none immediate, just need internal approval for peering.
[08:02] Maya: great. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the demo and a shared drive with docs.
[08:09] Priya: i'll also attach a short checklist for KMS key rotation and HSM notes.
[08:15] Jon: and i'll start provisioning the staging namespace tomorrow and share creds with ibrahim when ready.
[08:22] (end of substantive discussion; rest is wrap-up)
[08:30] Maya: thanks everyone. next meeting: control plane demo scheduled tentatively 2027-07-21 — i'll confirm.
[08:38] Sofia: thanks all.
[08:40] Derek: appreciate it.
[08:43] Maya: bye everyone.
